key_insight: Dual-band mid-infrared absorption imaging maps ethylene concentration and temperature in a Mach-2 cavity using simpler spectral instrumentation than hyperspectral imaging.
engineering_relevance: Spatially resolved fuel and temperature measurements help diagnose supersonic fuel mixing and shock-driven changes in cavity fueling.
method: Pair a broadband infrared source and high-frame-rate camera with two narrowband filters having different temperature sensitivities.
Use temperature-dependent, filter-weighted absorption cross-sections to infer two-dimensional ethylene number density and temperature.
Use a complementary temperature-independent single-band filter for instantaneous concentration imaging at 100 Hz.
evidence_signal: Across cavity, curtain, and discrete injection configurations, cavity equivalence ratios agreed well with independent extractive measurements, while single-band imaging revealed intermittent fueling reductions associated with shock-induced plume deflection.
watch_item: The reported 100 Hz concentration measurements used the single-band implementation; equivalent time-resolved dual-band temperature performance is not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Dual-Band Mid-Infrared Imaging for Measurement of Fuel Concentration and Temperature in a Supersonic Cavity
